item.title: Make listItems follow cursor pages
item.brief: In this repository (inventory-client), change listItems(transport) so it resolves to every item in order by following next_cursor until it is null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged; the first request sends no cursor. Keep the existing signature. Add or update tests with a fake transport that serves multiple pages, checking order, cursor passing, a single-page response, and an empty result. Do not hide errors: a failed page request must reject. Update the README to document the pagination behaviour. Run npm test and make it pass. Commit locally on the current branch with a clear message and the trailer from the contract. Do not push. Do not touch inventory-api.

pr.summary: listItems now returns every item across pages. Before: only the first page of GET /items. Now: follows next_cursor until null or absent, rejects on failed page or repeated cursor.

agt_01M8AX5S0FXCHAJAPZKZE4H5BD:1.description: Repeated-cursor check only compares next_cursor with the immediately previous cursor, so a cycle A->B->A (or any longer cycle) is not detected and listItems loops forever. README promises such a repeat rejects. Reproduced: 51 requests, no rejection. Fix: keep a Set of seen cursors and reject on any repeat; add a test with a 2-cycle. at client.js:25

agt_01M8AX5S0FXCHAJAPZKZE4H5BD:2.description: The repeated-cursor test only covers an immediate self-repeat (same -> same), so it does not exercise the multi-page cycle case. Add an A->B->A test once the guard is fixed. at test/client.test.js:79

agt_01M8AX5S0FXCHAJAPZKZE4H5BD:3.description: If a page body is null or not an object, body.items throws a bare TypeError instead of the descriptive 'without an items array' error. Still rejects, so it is only a message-quality issue. at client.js:19

agt_01M8AX71E82TAMH5A1S5DJ6MA0:1.description: seenCursors.add(cursor) also runs when cursor is undefined on the final page. The has() check is guarded by cursor !== undefined, so this is harmless. Guarding the add the same way would make the intent clearer.

risk.why: One function in client.js plus tests and README. Behaviour change is the intended pagination; valid paging unaffected. npm test 12/12. Re-review passed with one non-blocking nit.

Assumptions and limits: breaking change by design, since the default page size is 20. Non-canonical cursors are accepted (non-blocking). get_item over-long id crash is pre-existing and out of scope. inventory-client is not changed here.

agt_01M8AX737A4GGFZH68NEGKBYWH:3.description: api.py uses bare assert statements for runtime invariants on the request path. They vanish under python -O and add nothing that the code does not already guarantee. Remove them or turn them into tests.

agt_01M8AX77PVE9GW6BR9S1TF98DX:1.description: api.py `_decode_cursor`: the `int(text)` call sits outside the try/except that converts errors to BadRequest. A valid-base64 cursor that decodes to more than 4300 ASCII digits (Python 3.14 int-conversion limit) raises an uncaught ValueError, so GET /items crashes instead of returning 400 {"error": ...}. Probe: cursor = urlsafe_b64encode(b"9"*5000) gives ValueError: Exceeds the limit (4300 digits).

agt_01M8AX77PVE9GW6BR9S1TF98DX:2.description: Cursors are not canonical. Non-canonical base64 such as "MQ==" with padding, and decoded text such as "0005" or "0", are accepted as valid cursors. A well-formed cursor for a number that is not an item id (e.g. encoding 1000) returns 200 with an empty page instead of 400 'unrecognised cursor', as the brief literally asks. Decide whether to accept this or to validate the cursor against the item ids

agt_01M8AX77PVE9GW6BR9S1TF98DX:3.description: api.py lines 41-42 use `assert` for runtime checks in request-handling code. These are stripped under `python -O`, and they add no value because the logic is already correct. Remove them or replace them with a test.

agt_01M8AX7CAQJW6D4YQ0SSPFCNSE:1.description: A well-formed cursor that names no item is accepted with HTTP 200 instead of 400. _decode_cursor only checks that the decoded text is digits, so base64 of "9999" or "0" is treated as a valid after-id. The README says an unrecognised cursor returns 400, and the spec says the same, so code and docs disagree. test_invalid_cursor only covers malformed cursors, so nothing catches this. Probe, in a mkte

agt_01M8AX7CAQJW6D4YQ0SSPFCNSE:2.description: The three assert statements in list_items are redundant (the slice guarantees the length bound and the filter guarantees the id bound) and add noise to a minimal diff. They are also stripped under python -O, so they are not real guards.

agt_01M8AX9SX65NFKCHZ5CS9WW8KZ:2.description: Uncaught ValueError on an overlong limit: _parse_limit calls int(raw) outside any try block. Probe limit='9'*5000 raises ValueError 'Exceeds the limit (4300 digits)' on Python 3.14.7 instead of returning 400. Pre-existing in base 86e859f (line unchanged by delta), but it is the documented invalid-limit path and the delta does not fix it.

agt_01M8AXCC0C94JMMNKDM1CG91DT:2.description: Pre-existing, out of scope: get_item calls int(raw_id) without a guard, so an overlong numeric id raises ValueError. The delta does not touch get_item, so this is not a regression from this change.

Probe, in a mkte

agt_01M8AX7CAQJW6D4YQ0SSPFCNSE:2.description: The three assert statements in list_items are redundant (the slice guarantees the length bound and the filter guarantees the id bound) and add noise to a minimal diff. They are also stripped under python -O, so they are not real guards.

agt_01M8AX9SX65NFKCHZ5CS9WW8KZ:2.description: Uncaught ValueError on an overlong limit: _parse_limit calls int(raw) outside any try block. Probe limit='9'*5000 raises ValueError 'Exceeds the limit (4300 digits)' on Python 3.14.7 instead of returning 400. Pre-existing in base 86e859f (line unchanged by delta), but it is the documented invalid-limit path and the delta does not fix it.

agt_01M8AX9SX65NFKCHZ5CS9WW8KZ:3.description: Pre-existing, outside the delta: get_item does int(raw_id) after isdigit() with no guard, so GET /items/<5000 digits> raises uncaught ValueError on Python 3.14.7 instead of 400. Same class as reviewer-delta:1.

agt_01M8AXCC0C94JMMNKDM1CG91DT:2.description: Pre-existing, out of scope: get_item calls int(raw_id) without a guard, so an overlong numeric id raises ValueError. The delta does not touch get_item, so this is not a regression from this change.

agt_01M8AXF3VPCY066CMMWQE9034G:1.description: Non-canonical cursor encodings are accepted: base64 of '0005' (MDAwNQ==) decodes to id 5 and returns 200 with a page starting at item 6. Still open from agt_01M8AX77PVE9GW6BR9S1TF98DX:2 (canonicality part). at api.py:70

agt_01M8AXF3VPCY066CMMWQE9034G:2.description: get_item still raises an uncaught ValueError for an overlong all-digit id (e.g. '9'*5000), because int() runs after isdigit with no guard. Pre-existing and untouched by this change. Still open from agt_01M8AX9SX65NFKCHZ5CS9WW8KZ:3 and agt_01M8AXCC0C94JMMNKDM1CG91DT:2. at api.py:81

agt_01M8AXF3VPCY066CMMWQE9034G:3.description: An empty cursor (cursor=) returns 400 rather than being treated as absent. Behaviour is consistent with the contract but not stated in the README. at api.py:45

agt_01M8AXF3VPCY066CMMWQE9034G:4.description: No test covers non-canonical cursor encodings or the known-id check that rejects numbers outside the item set. Test coverage gap only. at test_api.py:48
